newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs pare losses on short covering.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs pare losses on short covering.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese interest rate and government bonds futures pared losses late Tuesday after the yen surged against the U.S. dollar in Asia, dealers said.
Earlier reports that Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) would recommend a rise in the discount rate triggered stop-loss selling in Euroyen futures.
"Officials have denied that and there's been some covering back since," a European commission house dealer said, adding that higher rates would only serve to boost the yen further.
The December Euroyen contract was at 98.96 at 1115 GMT compared with the IMM's 98.97 and up from a low of 98.92.
The dollar took a dive below 112 yen in late Asia for the first time since December 6 on speculation the Fed would leave U.S. rates unchanged after its policy meeting on Tuesday.
Unchanged U.S. interest rates against higher Japanese rates were seen likely to worsen Japan's trade surplus with the U.S.
Japanese government bond futures also pared losses boosted by the yen's surge versus the dollar.
Dealers said the market was also unfazed by talk of a rate hike as any recommendations would take time to implement.
June settled at 124.45 against 124.48 previously, up from 124.27. It was seen trekking up to test 125.50 on the topside.
Elsewhere, Eurodollars marked time ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday.
Dealers said the tendency was to square positions but the market was leaning towards the view that the FOMC would not change rates as growth was not so robust.
This was evident in a fair amount of spread buying of nearby months for forward, as a rate hike was expected to occur later in the year, possibly after September.
September Eurodollars ended at 93.875 against their IMM close at 93.885, while December ended at 93.670 against 93.675.
